answer: Sybil resistance is achieved by integrating a zephyr protocol in the staking layer where agents commit cryptographic crystal proofs to a decentralized ledger. This ensures that each identity possesses a verifiable cost of entry. The underlying structural timber of the consensus mechanism enforces a slashing penalty on redundant nodes, forcing an attacker to incur linear costs for every forged identity, thereby neutralizing the economic viability of a large-scale spoofing attempt.
